2.3.4 Scientific Publications/Communications

During the fellowship we have been able to successfully develop and publish several articles
(List of the publication in the appendix 3). I attended also the 8th EDCTP Forum and
presented a poster entitled:

M. Siribie, A.B Tiono, A.G.A Babiker, A. Sanou, L. Sermé, Z. Gansané, A. Traoré, M.F
Gomes, F. Pagnoni and S.B Sirima. Impact of an Integrated Community Case Management
of Fever/Malaria and Pneumonia on Child Mortality: a Cluster - Randomized Controlled Trial
in Burkina Faso. Poster Communication. 8th EDCTP Forum, 6-9 November 2016, Lusaka,
Zambia.

2.4 Networking Opportunities
As young scientist, this fellowship programme was an opportunity to look for networking
opportunities as well, for our professional support. First of all, it will be a tremendous support
for me to be able to keep connexion with my host institution (IVI) after the fellowship scheme
for the contribution to the ongoing clinical research activities and the conduct of future clinical
research activities in Africa.
Moreover, we have some promising exchanges going on for networking opportunities as
follow:

-­‐ Between former and current EDCTP – TDR CRS fellows and in collaboration with the
Luxembourg Institute of Health and the University of Copenhagen, we submitted a

letter of intent to the EDCTP Call for clinical research 2016: “Clinical trials and
operational research studies to optimize the use of products for poverty
related diseases in mothers, new-borns, children and/or adolescents”. We
are waiting for the notification of the review committee by the end of
December 2016 and to proceed with the next, which will consist of the
development and submission of the full proposal.
-­‐ With the Head of the Department of Public Health Medicine, School of Public Health,
University of Bielefeld in Germany, we are planning to initiate a collaborative clinical
research after the end of my fellowship on Climate change and Infectious Diseases.
-­‐ With the Chief of the Department of the vaccines preventable diseases, Public Health
Agency of Canada, we are planning a surveillance study of some vaccine preventable
diseases in Burkina Faso.
-­‐ With the Head of Enteric Diseases of the “Agence the Médecine Preventive (AMP)”,
Paris, France for opportunities for collaborative activities in the near future.
